## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 7*, entitled *Dutiyasaṁghikacetāpana* ("Exchanging designated Sangha property that was asked for"), is an expiation-with-forfeiture rule in the Theravāda nun's Vinaya. The rule provides that when a nun solicits a requisite intended for the Saṅgha that has been allocated for a specific purpose and then exchanges it for another item, she commits an offense entailing forfeiture of the requisite and confession. Bhikkhu Brahmali has provided a modern English translation of the text.

 Curated parallels include the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-np7*) and Bhikkhunī Parivāra, alongside the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Np 21*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Np 26*), Mūlasarvāstivāda in both Chinese and Tibetan (*Lzh Mu Bi Vb Np 29*, *xct-mu-bi-vb-np29*), Mahāsaṅghika (*Lzh Mg Bi Vb Np 13*), and the Sanskrit Mahāsaṅghika-Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇī Vinaya* (*san-lo-bi-vb-np13*).
